What it shows: which oxygen and pressure conditions PSI experiments actually tested. Each dot is one test (color = investigation, triangle = O₂ measured in the burner stream). Empty areas are conditions with no test data, so any conclusion there would be an extrapolation. The shaded box is the lunar-habitat reference: at least 30% O₂ at or below 10.2 psi.

Chart clicks snap to a display grid. Type oxygen and pressure in the copilot for exact conditions.

How to use it with the copilot: click anywhere on the chart to choose a habitat condition (the dark-cyan marker and the copilot's Oxygen and Pressure fields follow your click; you can also type the values). Then press Ask copilot: the application ranks the investigations closest to that point, and the language model explains the ranking using only cited records and report passages. Dots near the marker mean well-covered conditions; a marker in an empty area means the answer rests on distant tests. The ranking is not only distance: it weighs five criteria (O₂ closeness, pressure closeness, fire-safety pillar, fuel type, data richness), so a study can rank high with few dots near the marker. After you ask, the studies in the answer stay highlighted and the rest fade.
